Whopping $1.818 mil transacted price for a Dawson five-room flat — all-time high in Singapore per HDB data
article:
A five-room flat in Queenstown just set a fresh islandwide record for HDB resale prices — by absolute quantum and on a psf basis — when it was resold at $1.818 million ($1,521 psf) on Oct 30, going by HDB’s resale flat database.

Located at Block 96 Dawson Road , part of the SkyParc @ Dawson development, the unit sits on the 40th to 42nd storeys and measures 111 sq m (1,194.8 sq ft). It has a remaining lease of around 94 years.

Ted Wong of ERA Realty Network, who was the appointed agent for the seller, told EdgeProp Singapore that the unit overlooks the expansive greenery of the Dempsey area and saw high demand from prospective buyers.

"More than eight offers were received, with the top three all above $1.8 million," Wong said.

He added that interested parties valued the centrality of the location, abundant amenities nearby, the view of the greenery, and the ample size of the unit.

In Wong’s view, the “relatively low” supply of five-room flats in the estate also contributed to the level of interest and the record-breaking outcome.

The price tag of $1.818 million surpasses the previous HDB resale record of $1.728 million , set in April 2026 when a five-room flat at Block 96A Henderson Road , part of City Vue @ Henderson in Bukit Merah, changed hands. That unit is located on the 46th to 48th floor and spans 113 sq m (1,216 sq ft). Its psf price works out to $1,421.

On a psf basis, the latest SkyParc @ Dawson flat transaction also exceeds the previous islandwide high of $1,502 psf , set in September 2026. That involved a 1,065 sq ft, five-room flat at the neighbouring Block 91 Dawson Road , part of SkyTerrace @ Dawson , which had fetched $1.6 million.

Within Queenstown, the previous record by absolute price was $1.7 million, held by a five-room flat sold in February this year at Block 92 Dawson Road , which is also at SkyTerrace @ Dawson.

At the time, the $1.7 million transaction was the most expensive transacted HDB flat in Singapore.

Source: EdgeProp Buddy , HDB

Completed in 2020, SkyParc @ Dawson serves as a replacement project under the Selective En bloc Redevelopment Scheme (Sers) for residents from Tanglin Halt.

title: SpaceX: Rocketing Past Expectations on AI and Starlink Performance
article:
SpaceX 3Q2026 Core Segment & Company Summary

Key Highlights & Growth Drivers

Core profit engine; consumer subscribers rose 88.9% YoY and Starlink Mobile reached >22 million users.
Consolidated SpaceX
US$14.58 billion (+161% YoY)
US$2.79 billion operating profit (Net: US$4.40 billion)
First profitable public quarter; backed by US$63 billion backlog and US$51 billion net cash position.
Space Exploration Technologies Corp
. (NASDAQ: SPCX), or SpaceX, has posted its first profitable quarter as a listed company in its third-quarter 2026 (3Q2026) results.
The reason?
A blowout quarter beyond consensus estimates, with
artificial intelligence (AI)
and Starlink doing the heavy lifting.
A Profitable Turn
SpaceX’s 3Q2026 revenue surged 161% year on year (YoY) to US$14.58 billion, while net income flipped from a US$1.05 billion loss to a US$4.40 billion profit, driven by rapid growth in Starlink’s customer base and higher revenue contributions from the Super Intelligence (SI) segment.
The surge in AI rental revenue has won over some analysts, but not all.
Morningstar raised its fair-value estimate for SpaceX but still considers the shares significantly overvalued, trading at roughly twice that estimate.
These improved results are landing SpaceX on growth investors’ watchlists.
Super Intelligence: The New Top-Line Powerhouse
SpaceX’s SI (previously AI) segment delivered a superb 3Q2026 performance, with revenue rising 829.9% YoY to US$7.56 billion, swinging from an operating loss of US$1.72 billion to an operating profit of US$431 million.
Large Grok Enterprise (including Cursor) customer accounts within the SI division – those that already generate over US$1 million in annual run-rate revenue – grew 50% quarter on quarter (QoQ) on a pro forma basis.
Remarkably, the SI segment now generates 51.9% of total net sales, surpassing satellite connectivity as the largest revenue contributor.
Crucially, it’s showing no signs of slowing.
While its active compute capacity reached 1.7 gigawatts (GW) as of 30 September 2026, management targets between 2.5 GW and 3.0 GW by the end of 2026 and around 13 GW by the end of 2027.
To sweeten the deal, management says the newly deployed compute is paying back its cost in less than a year at current rental prices.
That is a sign that, for now, demand is keeping pace with SpaceX’s build-out.
Related articles:
Missed the AI Boom? Here’s How Investors Can Still Benefit from the Next Wave
3 Singapore Stocks Quietly Profiting from the AI Boom
Starlink’s Profitability
While SI dominates the headlines, SpaceX’s Starlink and launch segments provide steady growth and space supremacy, respectively.
Revenue from the Connectivity segment, which houses Starlink, rose 69.5% YoY to US$5.20 billion, supported by an 88.9% jump in consumer subscribers and a US$1.02 billion increase in enterprise and government revenue, led by Starshield (its US government business) and airline installations.
Although average revenue per user (ARPU) for consumers fell 16.9% YoY to US$69 a month, the bigger subscriber base more than made up for it, with consumer revenue up 57%.
Starlink Mobile, its satellite-to-mobile broadband service, performed well, with monthly active users surging 37% QoQ to more than 22 million.
Generating $2.37 billion in operating profit at a 45.1% margin, the Connectivity segment remains SpaceX’s biggest profit engine.
Space Supremacy
SpaceX’s Space Operations 3Q2026 revenue rose 6.1% YoY to US$1.77 billion despite launches falling from 44 to 35, helped by a more favourable mix of customer missions.
That said, the segment slipped to a small operating loss of US$7 million, from a US$259 million profit a year ago, as SpaceX ramped up spending on Starship development.
Notably, SpaceX successfully sent Starship – its towering next-generation rocket – into orbit for the first time on Flight 14 and delivered 26 of its latest Starlink V3 satellites, marking a major milestone.
According to Starlink, a single V3 satellite provides ten and twenty-two times the downlink and uplink capacity, respectively, compared with a V2 satellite, potentially reducing its cost per unit bandwidth, which could in turn drive future margin expansion.
Explosive Guidance vs. Spending Realities
SpaceX reiterated its target of US$100 billion in annualised revenue run rate (ARR) by the end of 2026, while CEO Elon Musk suggested ARR could reach $500 billion to $1 trillion by end-2027, a five- to tenfold increase within a year.
This comes after increased visibility into SpaceX’s compute contract pipeline over the next six months.
Its massive backlog of US$63 billion, of which $42 billion is expected to be recognised within twelve months, also bolstered management’s optimism.
However, behind the rosy guidance lies an immense capital commitment.
Beyond its compute hardware and power build-out, SpaceX is also constructing Starbase, Louisiana.
The new spaceport is designed to handle thousands of Starship flights a year, with its first launch targeted for 2029.
In the first nine months of 2026 (9M2026), its operating cash flow and capital expenditure (capex) stood at US$13.10 billion and US$48.07 billion, respectively, pushing its free cash flow (FCF) into the red.
With its fourth quarter 2026 (4Q2026) capex projected to spike from US$19.59 billion in 3Q2026 to between $35 billion and $40 billion, its negative FCF is expected to worsen.
As of 30 September 2026, SpaceX maintained a decent
balance sheet
, supported by a favourable current ratio of 3.08x and a net cash position of US$51 billion, providing a cushion against its cash burn.
Related articles:
AI Boom or Bust? Here Are 4 Telltale Signs
Temasek Doubles Down on AI: 3 Powerhouse Stocks You Could Consider in Your Portfolio
Get Smart: The Takeaway for Growth Investors
SpaceX delivered its first profitable quarter as a listed company, powered by its SI and Starlink divisions.
Management’s outlook, including 1Q2027 revenue guidance of US$33 billion to US$37 billion, suggests this growth is set to continue.
While rising capex drags down its FCF, raising investor concerns, SpaceX’s sub-one-year payback on new compute at current pricing, alongside its massive backlog, should not be ignored.
Anchoring the space economy, SpaceX sits at the unique intersection of orbital infrastructure and artificial intelligence – an unmatched
competitive advantage
.
However, investors should size their positions carefully, given SpaceX’s increasingly intense capital spending.
Not all AI “winners” will survive this cycle.

title: AI darling Taiwan’s blowout growth extends run unseen since 1987
article:
(Oct 30): Taiwan reported its fourth straight quarter of double-digit economic growth, the longest such stretch in nearly 39 years, as the artificial intelligence (AI) boom increasingly spills over into stronger domestic demand.

Gross domestic product (GDP) expanded 14.36% in the third quarter from a year earlier, according to a statement from the statistics bureau in Taipei on Friday. That exceeded all but one forecast in a Bloomberg survey of economists, whose median estimate was 12%.

Gross capital formation, a measure of investment used to calculate GDP, surged over 26% — the most in five years — with growth in private consumption holding above 5%.

Home to key suppliers of tech giants like Nvidia Corp and Apple Inc, Taiwan has been one of the biggest beneficiaries of the spread of AI.

The island’s exports surged almost 61% to a record of over US$87 billion ($111 billion) in September, beating the forecasts of all economists surveyed by Bloomberg.

See also: Lagarde downplays inflation risk as ECB holds, announces her early exit

Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Co, the world’s largest contract maker of advanced chips, also delivered a better-than-expected revenue outlook for the fourth quarter after reporting a 69% jump in profit for July to September, even as concerns persist over whether the AI investment boom can be sustained.

The rapid expansion has also bolstered Taiwan’s public finances. The cabinet proposed a record NT$3.93 trillion (US$120 billion or $150 billion) spending plan for 2027, giving the government more room to fund priorities including defence. Under the proposal, overall military spending would exceed 3% of GDP.

title: BP profit hits 18-year high as oil refining margins surge
article:
(Oct 30): BP plc said profit surged to the highest in 18 years as soaring refining margins boosted earnings, while a sharp drop in net debt moved the British energy major closer to a position where it could restart buybacks.

Adjusted net income was US$8.46 billion ($10.81 billion), up from US$2.21 billion a year earlier, the London-based giant said in a statement on Friday. More than half the profit came from the unit that includes oil refining and trading.

The results are chief executive officer Meg O’Neill’s second full quarter at the helm and offer a fresh look at the operational performance that she’s identified as a priority. BP’s first outsider CEO is cutting costs, selling assets and paying down debt while preparing to lay out her longer-term strategy for the firm in December.

“It really was a banner quarter for the refining business,” she said in an interview with Bloomberg TV. “We had very strong margins from the BP-operated refineries, we also had very strong underlying performance. We were able to capture the opportunity provided by the market.”

Net debt tumbled to US$13.87 billion from US$22.3 billion just three months earlier, surpassing the company’s target a year ahead of schedule. The rapid improvement in BP’s balance sheet gives O’Neill more room to consider shareholder returns after the company suspended buybacks earlier this year to prioritise paying down debt.

BP made no new announcement about share repurchases on Friday. Still, the collapse in net debt removes a key constraint on distributions at a time when surging refining profits are showering the industry with cash.

See also: Oil surges on signs US may resume military strikes against Iran

The profit surge comes amid a refining boom that’s showering Europe’s oil giants with cash, spurring BP’s rivals to announce jumbo payouts to investors.

Wars involving Iran and Russia have knocked out or disrupted oil refineries and trade routes, squeezing the world’s capacity to turn crude into diesel, gasoline and jet fuel. That’s driving up prices for consumers while handing outsized profits to plants that remain operational.

On Thursday, rival Shell plc announced it was increasing its quarterly share buyback to US$5 billion from US$3 billion after its refining margins surged and earnings climbed to their highest since the aftermath of Russia’s full-scale invasion of Ukraine. TotalEnergies SE has pledged as much as US$2.5 billion of repurchases this quarter, while Repsol SA and Eni SpA have also boosted their buybacks.

See also: Bangladesh in talks to buy more American gas, says US ambassador

The company’s adjusted net income beat the US$7.3 billion average analyst estimate compiled by Bloomberg. BP said oil and gas trading operations both performed strongly. It was the highest since the third quarter of 2008.

BP’s major’s refining margin indicator surged to US$46.70 a barrel during the quarter from US$29.60 in the previous period.

The company’s Customer and Products unit, where oil trading and refining sit, made US$4.8 billion in the quarter. It made US$5.3 billion in all of 2025.

BP expects oil and gas production to fall slightly in the fourth quarter due to continued Middle East disruption and other impacts elsewhere.

“Every division came in ahead of consensus expectations, supported by some solid operational indicators in the upstream and downstream, as well as another strong quarter for the trading business,” RBC analyst Biraj Borkhataria said in a note on Friday.

title: Nvidia CEO says ties to Singapore company in spy probe were ‘normal’
article:
(Oct 30): Nvidia Corp chief executive officer Jensen Huang said the chipmaker’s dealings with Megaspeed International were “normal and not unusual” following a New York Times report that one of the Singapore firm’s executives is under investigation for spying on behalf of China.

Nvidia’s relationship with Megaspeed’s officials was proper, and the chipmaker has checked to ensure that Megaspeed didn’t illegally send its artificial intelligence (AI) processors to China, Huang said in an interview Thursday. That country is barred from buying Nvidia’s powerful AI chips — known as graphics processing units, or GPUs — under US export rules.

“We’ve studied all their deployments of our GPUs and counted every one,” he said in the interview. “And I think the US government also has as well.”

The remarks follow a Times story that the US government is investigating an executive from Megaspeed for allegedly providing information to the Chinese government. Huang Le has previously been pictured with Nvidia’s leader on social media, and the story reports that she may have been serving as a Chinese agent aiming to evade chip export controls.

Asked about the report at a regular daily briefing in Beijing, Chinese Foreign Ministry spokesman Guo Jiakun said it was “unsubstantiated and purely a smear against China”.

In the interview, Huang said that his interactions with her were typical of those with Chinese customers and executives. She’s no longer with Megaspeed, he said.

See also: Neocloud troubles won’t end the AI boom

“Our relationship, our interactions, have been related to Megaspeed, and it was all completely normal and not unusual,” Huang said. The CEO said he hadn’t been informed by the US government of its suspicions about Huang Le.

The growing geopolitical rivalry between the US and China has led to increasing clampdowns by Washington on exports of key American technology. That’s cut off Nvidia from a lucrative source of revenue in China, the largest market for chips.

The company has received some latitude to ship a limited amount of older AI-related products to the Asian country under the Trump administration. That approval hasn’t resulted in a material amount of shipments, at least in part because Beijing has sought to limit the deliveries itself in an effort to foster its own chip industry.

See also: INSEAD gets US$3 mil from Google.org and DeepMind to study AI’s effect on work

Nonetheless, the restrictions on exports have led to investigations and charges of smuggling of Nvidia’s best products to China — something the company has said is an insignificant issue. Megaspeed is one of a group of companies that Bloomberg News and others have reported may have tried to illegally divert shipments of chips intended for data centres outside of China into that country.

title: Record Binance hack shows no crypto firm is too big to breach
article:
(Oct 30): A security breach at Binance involving up to US$6.3 billion ($8.1 billion) is the biggest crypto hack on record, raising fresh questions about the industry’s ability to protect digital assets as it seeks to woo traditional finance.

The incident at the world’s largest crypto exchange highlights how vulnerabilities can extend even to the biggest players.

“This is the largest cyber theft on record, not just the largest in crypto,” said Aneirin Flynn, chief executive officer of cybersecurity technology firm FailSafe. “This will damage confidence in crypto. The industry is courting institutional capital, but institutions will not overlook repeated failures in custody and security.”

So far the total impact sits at around US$6.3 billion, Binance said in a post on X on Friday, adding that it will make good all losses. Binance has temporarily suspended withdrawals on the exchange.

The hack extends a string of costly breaches across the cryptocurrency industry. In February 2025, Dubai-based Bybit suffered a US$1.5 billion theft, then the largest single crypto heist on record. The FBI blamed North Korean hackers, who dispersed the stolen assets across thousands of addresses on multiple blockchains.

See also: Binance says US$6.3 bil impacted as crypto reels from hack

There have been several big heists in recent months.

In August, hackers absconded with more than US$100 million worth of bitcoin from thousands of wallets secured by hardware devices made by Canada-based Coinkite Inc. The attack exploited a software flaw that made the private keys protecting the crypto predictable.

In September, crypto exchange Bitget said attackers made off with about US$388 million. And in October, criminals tampered with Ledger hardware wallets distributed through a Southeast Asian reseller, with blockchain researchers estimating losses of more than US$90 million. Ledger said its own systems weren’t breached.

See also: Bitcoin dips below US$80,000 as AI-related market selloff deepens

Prediction market Polymarket temporarily halted trading this week after a third-party provider was compromised, with more than US$2.5 million lost.

The incidents highlight the breadth of vulnerabilities facing crypto businesses, from their own wallets and technology systems to supply chains and outside providers.

The risks extend beyond crypto-native companies. In South Korea, a series of cyberattacks has hit financial institutions in recent weeks, including cryptocurrency exchange Bithumb Co, Mirae Asset Global Investments Co and Daishin Securities Co reporting unauthorised access that exposed user data.

The breaches have raised questions about the security of outsourced systems and third-party technology providers as financial firms increasingly rely on interconnected digital infrastructure.

“Every bank, asset manager and exchange operator trying to put treasuries, funds or equities on-chain has to pick a settlement layer, and until tonight ‘the biggest exchange’ was a defensible answer,” said Luca Parlamento, founder and chief investment officer at D2 Finance. “Now it’s an unsecured credit decision.” D2 Finance doesn’t have any transactions on Binance, Parlamento said.

Initial investigation suggests that the security incident may involve an engineer’s compromised laptop, Binance said in its post.

To stay ahead of Singapore and the region’s corporate and economic trends, click here for Latest Section

According to blockchain analytics firm TRM Labs, North Korea is behind the hack. It said preparation started at least 36 hours before the theft.

“On the evening of October 29, billions of dollars in crypto began leaving wallets belonging to Binance” across 10 blockchains — including bitcoin, ethereum, solana and XRP — and flowing to addresses controlled by a single attacker, TRM said.

For exchanges holding billions of dollars in customer assets, the challenge is no longer simply securing private keys or keeping most funds in offline storage. Wallet systems increasingly involve multiple signers, automated transaction processes, smart-contract permissions and external service providers.

“The lesson for an allocator isn’t that crypto is risky. It’s that an exchange balance is an unsecured loan to a company that can lose its keys,” Parlamento said.

title: When Intel sneezes, AEM catches a cold
article:
The best thing about Mainboard-listed AEM Holdings (SGX:AWX ) is also the worst thing about it. The local chip-testing company has been riding high on the global AI boom. That has allowed AEM’s stock price to go up by more than seven-fold over the past year, hitting a peak of $11.58.

But tying one’s fortunes to a single factor makes it a single point of risk. These days, investors are beginning to question the value of all the capital tech companies have been pouring into AI. Google’s parent company, Alphabet endured a blood bath on Oct 29, losing US$500 billion in market value, after reporting its second consecutive quarter of negative free cash flow.

The past few weeks have been a period of reckoning for AEM as well. AEM’s stock price has been trending downwards since Oct 9 when it was originally sitting at $11.18. The worst, however, had yet to come. AEM opened at $7.34 on Oct 30, nearly 10% lower than its closing price a day before. AEM’s shares were trading at $7.35 as at 3 pm.

That drubbing was not due to any disclosures from AEM itself. Afterall, the company had announced its earnings for 1HFY2026 less than three months ago on Aug 12. At the time, AEM had reported a whopping 876% y-o-y increase in its earnings to $30.8 million. Instead, the key driver behind AEM’s stock price plummet on Oct 30 might have been the underwhelming earnings announcement from one of its customers, Intel.

On Oct 29, Intel reported its earnings for 3QFY2026. The chip giant’s revenue for the third quarter was up 20% y-o-y at US$16.5 billion. While Intel says its revenue figure is US$0.2 billion above its outlook in July, it is still lower than the US$16.6 billion analysts were forecasting. What was even more troubling were the remarks made by Intel’s CEO Lip-Bu Tan on the poor outlook for central processing unit (CPU) sales.

“In recent weeks, our customers began signalling a PC slowdown based on memory prices and availability,” Tan told analysts during the company’s earnings call. “Year-to-date system end-point prices have increased significantly placing additional pressure on already limited IT budgets.”

See also: South Korea's FuriosaAI quadruples value to US$2.9 bil in Nvidia chase

According to Tan, the correction that has been taking place within the personal computer (PC) market has accelerated over the last two months. Intel’s original equipment manufacturer (OEM) partners have tried to match the softer sell thru by managing their inventory aggressively, Tan adds. He expects current market conditions to persist until memory availability and prices begin to normalise.

“I am disappointed that we were not able to meet strong customer demand in this quarter. We face near term challenges, including manufacturing supply shortages, the unprecedented memory crunch, and the resulting softness in PC demand,” Tan says.

Intel is a major customer of AEM. That means Intel’s bad news could very well be AEM’s bad news. To be clear, AEM does not reveal the amount of revenue it draws from Intel. In its annual report for FY2026, AEM said one customer from its test cell solutions segment was responsible for over $152 million out of the group’s total revenue of $399 million but it did not specify who that company was. That said, most analysts view Intel as a larger driver of AEM’s revenue. DBS Group Research analyst Amanda Tan said in a July 24 report on AEM that Intel accounts for about 25% of her FY2026 revenue forecast.

See also: Nvidia-backed firm launches US$3.1 bil GPU loan in market

Incidentally, Tan was still bullish on CPUs earlier this month. The Intel chief was speaking on a panel at DBS’s Asia Future Forward Conference on Oct 12 when he told attendees that CPUs were actually more useful than GPUs (graphic processing units) when it comes to certain aspects of AI training.

“We are excited [that] the CPU demand is so strong,” Tan says. “The CPU, actually, is more useful when you do the inference orchestrations and reinforcement learning. A lot of frontier model [companies], they have been asking, ‘Lip-Bu, we need more CPU.’ So, I think overall that is a positive for us.”

title: SNB reports nine-month profit on foreign currencies and gold
article:
(Oct 30): The Swiss National Bank reported a solid nine-month profit thanks to its foreign-currency portfolio and gold holdings.

The SNB earned 44.2 billion francs (US$5.4 billion) from January through September, it said in a statement on Friday. That raised the likelihood of a year-end payout to the Swiss government.

The central bank’s hoard of assets in foreign currencies — including its large equities portfolio — delivered a profit of 43.3 billion francs. The value of the gold held by the central bank increased by 1.2 billion francs.

Positions in Swiss francs generated a gain of 0.1 billion francs. Those earnings include negative interest charged on oversized commercial-bank reserves held at the SNB. Sight deposits exceeding a certain threshold are subject to this since the central bank cut its benchmark rate to zero last year.

The SNB’s results don’t influence monetary policy and are heavily influenced by asset price changes, with quarterly numbers often having little bearing on final result for the year.

They are however fiscally important for the federal government and Switzerland’s cantons, or states. In cases of annual losses, the central bank at times can’t make a payout, which is particularly painful for smaller Swiss regions.

See also: ECB’s Moulin sees policy as measured with most prices stable

title: ECB’s Moulin sees policy as measured with most prices stable
article:
(Oct 30): The European Central Bank (ECB) is responding in a measured way to inflation as most prices are stable and pressures are largely imported rather than driven by domestic factors, Governing Council member Emmanuel Moulin said.

At its meeting on Thursday, the central bank refrained from a third increase in borrowing costs since the Iran war pushed up energy prices. But officials discussed the possibility of a hike and president Christine Lagarde said the direction of travel for future policy is “clear.”

“Excluding energy and fresh produce, prices remain relatively stable. Similarly, we aren’t seeing spillover effects to salaries at this stage,” Moulin said in an interview with French newspaper La Montagne. “In the current situation, with inflation mainly imported, the ECB is adopting a measured approach.”

Moulin, who’s also governor of the Bank of France, said the ECB will continue to follow the inflation situation “very closely” and take action at future meetings depending on data it has.

He reiterated his opposition to French far-left presidential candidate Jean-Luc Mélenchon’s proposal to cancel or freeze sovereign debt held by the Bank of France. Moulin said doing so would create a balance-sheet hole and spark difficulties for the entire euro area, without any gain for public finances.

“France has never defaulted on its debt since 1797,” he said. “Talking about such a cancellation would not only achieve very little, but it is already costing us as it creates distrust toward our country.”

See also: Jio Platforms adds US$36 bil in value after India IPO surge

Moulin also said it’s not the ECB’s job to step into help France with its fiscal challenges, which have spooked investors in recent weeks, sparking a selloff of bonds and driving up borrowing costs.

“Our fiscal problems should be dealt with in France, notably by voting a budget that reduces the deficit,” he said. “That’s what will enable us to reassure investors on the direction the country is going.”

title: Indian AI firm seeks US$3 bil financing for Nvidia chips order — Bloomberg
article:
(Oct 30): Indian AI infrastructure firm AM Intelligence is seeking to raise as much as US$3 billion to fund a previously announced purchase of Nvidia Corp’s next-generation chips, according to people familiar with the matter, the latest sign that the technology’s boom is driving a debt binge.

The funding package for the company, established by the founders of renewable energy producer Greenko Group Plc, could comprise of bonds and bank loans, among others, said the people who asked not to be identified discussing private details.

The breakdown between the various options is still being finalised and the firm also expects to get US$300 million in advance payment from potential offtakers, the people said. Talks are still in the initial stages and terms could change.

A representative for AM Intelligence declined to comment. Nvidia didn’t respond to requests for comment.

The planned deal shows how the race to fund the AI infrastructure buildout in Asia and elsewhere is giving rise to increasingly layered financing structures, combining traditional bank lending with private capital and upfront commitments from customers as developers seek billions of dollars to secure the latest generation of processors.

Globally, the borrowing binge tied to the AI boom has flooded markets with more than US$650 billion of debt in less than two years, according to data compiled by Bloomberg.

See also: Google shares drop after 3Q sales miss reignites fears over AI

AM Intelligence said in August that it had ordered Vera Rubin chips under an US$8 billion project, as it seeks to become one of the first adopters of the advanced computing platform in Asia. The project is part of a broader plan to set up one-gigawatt of computing capacity. Its Hyderabad facility aims to run trillion-parameter AI models and next-generation agentic AI applications.An estimated US$90 billion in investment opportunity could emerge across India’s data centre value chain by fiscal year 2035, extending beyond capacity additions into related infrastructure and services, according to a KPMG report released in July.

title: Keppel REIT’s response on the acquisition of Keppel South Central
article:
I refer to your article “Keppel REIT’s latest acquisition yet another unfavourable deal for minorities”, published on Oct 26, 2026 and would like to set out why Keppel REIT Management believes the acquisition of Keppel South Central is in the interests of Keppel REIT and all its Unitholders.

In considering the acquisition, we have focused on both its near-term income contribution and its potential to create value for Unitholders over the longer term.

Leasing at Keppel South Central has been progressing well with committed leases and leases in the process of documentation increasing from 52.7% as of Sept 30, 2026 to approximately 60% as of mid-October 2026. A further 20% of space is also under negotiation1, providing good visibility on continued lease-up. This is supported by positive Singapore office market fundamentals, with Grade-A CBD office vacancy expected to drop to 3.8%2 by 2030 and rents continuing to grow amid limited new supply.

While leasing in terms of achieved rental rate is above the acquisition assumptions and continues to progress, the proposed arrangement3 with Keppel REIT’s sponsor, Keppel, provides Unitholders with income stability for a period of up to five years after completion of the transaction. Unlike conventional income support arrangements, it is backed by current rents at Keppel South Central, with the average rent of approximately $11.30 psf already above the $11.15 psf rent assumed under the arrangement. At the same time, there remains upside from continued lease-up, with the potential for higher rents as leasing progresses from the low-to-mid floors to the mid-to-high floors.

The acquisition is DPU-accretive on a pro forma basis at 2.01%4, after taking into account adjustments to reflect the significant portfolio movements over the past year. Even without these adjustments, the acquisition would remain DPU accretive at 1.81% based on actual FY2025 DPU.

Keppel REIT has a long track record of acquiring quality assets, which have contributed recurring income and capital appreciation over time. This year, Keppel REIT’s focus was on active asset management and realising divestments, with a view to optimise the portfolio and strengthen its balance sheet to better position Keppel REIT in its core markets.

The divestments of KR Ginza II in Japan and T Tower in Seoul, announced last quarter, were at good premiums to their latest valuations and our historical entry prices. With divestments on track, we began focusing on how the portfolio can be optimised to enhance DPU for Unitholders over the long term. The unit buyback plan5 referred to in the announcement on the divestment of T Tower was part of the enhancement but that would have limited effect on replacing the DPU contribution from the divestments.

Thus, as part of Keppel REIT’s portfolio optimisation, we considered the Keppel South Central opportunity carefully, cognisant that it is still in pre-stabilisation stage. High-quality Singapore CBD assets are usually tightly held and typically trade at low cap rates. At an agreed property value of $626.2 million6, equivalent to approximately $2,350 psf, Keppel REIT is acquiring at an attractive initial property yield of 4.3%. We believe the terms agreed for Keppel South Central, including the certainty of income for up to five years, are attractive for Keppel REIT.

Keppel REIT remains focused on delivering stable distributions and sustainable long-term total returns to all Unitholders and believes Keppel South Central will contribute meaningfully to that for many years to come.

1Refer to Keppel Ltd’s media release dated Oct, 20, 2026 titled “Keppel to divest 51% stake in Keppel South Central for about $611 million to Keppel REIT” for further details.

3Based on Keppel REIT’s arrangement with the Vendor for the transaction. Refer to the announcement titled “Proposed acquisition of 51.0% interest in Keppel South Central” for further details.

4Assumes the proposed acquisition of Keppel South Central and the divestments of T Tower and KR Ginza II had been completed on Jan 1, 2025 and taking into account certain adjustments. Refer to the announcement titled “Proposed acquisition of 51.0% interest in Keppel South Central” for further details.

5Subject to prevailing market conditions and applicable laws and regulations. Refer to the announcement titled “Keppel REIT to crystallise value through divestment of T Tower in Seoul” dated Sept 23, 2026.

6The agreed property value of Keppel South Central takes into account independent valuations conducted by Colliers International Consultancy & Valuation (Singapore) and CBRE, which were commissioned by the trustee of Keppel REIT and the Manager respectively. Keppel South Central was valued at $646.7 million and $652.0 million by Colliers and CBRE respectively as of Sept 30, 2026, including the income support arrangement.

Chua Hsien Yang is CEO of Keppel REIT Management, the manager of Keppel REIT

title: Mapletree Investments prepares for IPO early next year
article:
During Mapletree Pan Asia Commercial Trust’s (MPACT) results briefing, what stood out was a question by Mervin Song, real assets and REITs analyst at JP Morgan, on the IPO of Mapletree Investments. “Ahead of the sponsors' potential listing next year, is it time for a more radical change in MPACT’s strategy? Would management of MPACT recommend to the board and sponsors to consider splitting MPACT into two REITs: Mapletree Singapore Trust and Mapletree Outside Singapore Trust to unlock value?”

Sharon Lim, CEO of MPACT’s manager, said: “Anything about the broader strategy of the group — that should be redirected to the group.”

So, the cat is out of the bag. It appears that the REIT and analyst community are aware that Mapletree Investments is at an advanced stage of the IPO process.

A well-known analyst has joined Mapletree in a strategy role for the IPO, market watchers say.

Market watchers have also identifed the CEO and chairman of the potential IPO. The listed entity will comprise entirely of a fund management structure and own 10% to 15% of the REITs, market watchers say.

Mapletree Investments is likely to be split into a ListCo and an AssetCo. The ListCo will comprise the fee-generating activities of the REITs, private funds, joint ventures and development properties.

See also: Anthropic IPO may spark AI rally as short bets on tech pile up

Meanwhile, the AssetCo will hold the balance sheet assets of the REITs, private funds, JVs and development properties.

The ListCo will manage the assets in AssetCo.

The group CEO of ListCo will be Goh Chye Boon. Lily Ler (formerly CEO of Mapletree Industrial Trust Management), Wong Mun Hong, Chua Tiow Chye and Hiew Yoon Khong will be in the steering committee.

See also: Mi Material closes at $1.82 on first day of trading; Stabilisation manager bought 1.5 mil shares at IPO price of $1.80

When asked, a Mapletree Investments spokesperson says: "As a matter of policy, we do not comment on market rumours. Any material information, should it arise, will be communicated through the appropriate channels."

Other market watchers suggest that the potential IPO of Mapletree Investments is part of a broader strategy by Singapore Inc to revive the stock market. Notably, there have been rumblings of big listings such as PSA, Singapore Power and even Changi Airport Group, although this appears unlikely in the near term.

Specifically on MPACT, Lim said the manager is planning a substantive asset enhancement initiative (AEI) on VivoCity. “Our back of the house which is our drop-off point, can be turned to some form of a front. So much traffic passes there, it's quite a shame that it's technically a back of a house. The back of this house connects to our hypermarket and H&M. I think there is a lot of work that we can do to change the space and add a new cluster. We are at a very advanced drafting stage. We don't see big hurdles, but we have not tendered out to get all the numbers but it will provide positive ROI. We are trying to minimise disruption. But we need disruption before we can get the numbers,” Lim elaborates.

In an initial update, JP Morgan points out that the key positives included Mapletree Business City's committed occupancy rising to 95.4% from 94.3% in 1QFY2027 ended June 30 and 93% a year ago, with committed leases beginning to contribute from 3QFY2027.

VivoCity remained strong, with 2QFY2027 NPI up 5% y-o-y, committed occupancy at 100%, 1HFY2027 rental reversion of +15.0% and 2QFY2027 tenant sales growth of 3.3% y-o-y.

Finance expenses fell 14.4% y-o-y in 1HFY2027, helping limit the decline in DPU to 3.0% despite NPI falling 6.5%.

The update points to China's year-to-date (1HFY2027) rental reversion of -29.9% as a key negative. Festival Walk's rental reversion during the first half was -15.6%. Japan's committed occupancy was only 57.5% (+1.5% ppt q-o-q), reflecting the previously disclosed Fujitsu Makuhari non-renewal.

To stay ahead of Singapore and the region’s corporate and economic trends, click here for Latest Section

"Festival Walk's occupancy improved to 99.9% and tenant sales rose 3.7% y-o-y in 2QFY2027, but negative reversions (-15.6% in 1HFY2027, from -9.1% in 1QFY2027) remain a drag on income.

MPACT’s weighted average cost of debt edged up to 2.95% from 2.94% in 1QFY2027, and management said the scope for further finance-cost savings has narrowed as rates rise. Aggregate leverage also increased to 38.1% from 37.7% in 1QFY2027," JP Morgan says.

However, it retained its "overweight" rating on MPACT with a June 2027 target of $1.45.

title: Mi Material’s stabilisation manager announces cessation of price stabilisation action; share price down more than 14%
article:
Mi Material’s stabilisation manager, CGS International, announced that it has purchased 2.75 million shares on Oct 30 at a price range of between $1.76 and $1.80.

Following which, the stabilisation manager has purchased a total of 5 million shares since Mi Material's listing and has ceased price stabilisation action as of today.

“As the total number of shares which had been over-allotted in connection with the offering has been fully covered by the purchases made under the price stabilising action, the over-allotment option granted by Mi Technovation Berhad to Oversea-Chinese Banking Corporation Limited and CGS International Securities will not be exercised,” the announcement reads.

Mi Material’s IPO, dated Oct 28, was priced at $1.80 and saw an overall subscription rate of 2.2 times.

As at 1.01pm, shares of Mi Material were trading 26 cents lower, or 14.4% down at $1.54.

title: US-owned startup plans US$600 mil Malaysia rare-earth refinery
article:
(Oct 30): A US majority-owned startup plans to invest US$600 million in a rare-earth refinery in Malaysia, seeking to develop a new source of the critical minerals as Washington pushes to reduce its reliance on China.

DTEC Mineral and Metal Technology expects to set up the plant in the Southeast Asian country within the next three years, chief executive Officer Milan Perlly said in an interview. It became the first company to receive permission recently under Malaysia’s eased export rules to ship unprocessed rare-earth material to the US.

The project would support efforts by Malaysia and the US to develop new sources of rare earths outside China, which dominates the processing of the minerals. Rare earths are essential for products ranging from electric vehicles and electronics to wind turbines and advanced weapons.

“The larger goal is to make Malaysia the rare-earth elements processing hub for ionic clay in the region,” Perlly said.

Much of Malaysia’s identified rare-earth resources are found in so-called ion-adsorption clay deposits, where the elements are loosely bound to clay rather than locked in hard rock, potentially making them easier and cheaper to extract. They can contain sought-after heavy rare earths used in high-performance magnets and other advanced technologies.

DTEC Mineral’s first refinery would have capacity to process 5,000 metric tons of rare-earth material annually, Perlly said. The company ultimately aims to build two facilities in Malaysia with combined capacity of 10,000 tons a year.

See also: Light at the end of the tunnel for KL’s 8 Conlay?

“The US wants us to build 10,000 metric tons output,” he said. “My goal is to put one plant on the east coast for 5,000 metric tons, a second plant on the west coast.”

DTEC Mineral is considering locations after holding talks with officials in the Malaysian states of Kedah, Terengganu, Perak and Negeri Sembilan, he said. The facilities would expand Malaysia’s role in the rare-earth industry beyond the processing operations of Australia’s Lynas Rare Earths Ltd., which runs a major plant in Pahang state.

DTEC Mineral intends to develop locally sourced ionic-clay deposits and eventually operate its own mine in Malaysia, Perlly said. Malaysia has identified an estimated 16.1 million tons of rare-earth resources, according to government estimates, much of which has yet to be proven commercially viable.

See also: Menara Tun Perak, Maybank’s former Kuala Lumpur headquarters, up for sale: sources

The company is preparing to ship about 30 tons of unprocessed rare-earth material to the US for research after receiving approval to export as much as 700 tons, he said. The shipment is intended to help determine the composition of the material and the most suitable processing technology, according to Perlly.

Perlly, a Malaysian-born US citizen who formerly worked at Capital One, and business partner David Greer own 51% of DTEC Mineral. Malaysian firm DTEC Engineering and Construction holds the remaining 49%.

DTEC Mineral has ambitions to list in Malaysia and on either the Nasdaq or New York Stock Exchange, Perlly said.

The firm was part of a trade and critical minerals pact signed between US President Donald Trump and Malaysian Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim last year. Under the agreement, DTEC is eligible for funding from Export–Import Bank of the United States, US International Development Finance Corporation and the Department of Defense, according to DTEC’s website.
